title: Individual response to exercise training - a statistical perspective
authors: Hecksteden A, Kraushaar J, Scharhag-Rosenberger F, Theisen D, Senn S, Meyer T
population: Statistical and methodological perspective on exercise-training response research
findings: Measurement error limits the accuracy of individual response estimates; at the individual level a low signal-to-noise ratio may not be compensated by increasing sample size.
Within-subject variation in training efficacy may contribute to gross response variability and cannot be disclosed by comparison with a control group; it calls for repeated interventions.

Response is influenced by a multitude of determinants, and indications of interaction between them lead to the hypothesis that an interactive rather than additive approach may give optimal predictive accuracy.
Conclusive inference and optimal prediction of subject-by-training interaction entail demanding statistical requirements beset with practical difficulties; pragmatic alternatives are warranted.
limitations: Conceptual statistical paper without original data; provides no ready-made predictive model or response-classification thresholds.
implications: Treat a single test or block as a noisy measure of response: require repeated comparable measurements before changing an athlete's model parameters or labelling a responder.
Use smoothing or shrinkage toward population priors when updating individual fitness or load-tolerance parameters from sparse data, and show uncertainty.
Do not hard-code a responder classification; keep the individual adaptation signal as a soft, confidence-weighted adjustment.

verification.notes: Crossref: title, J Appl Physiol, issued 2015-06-15, first author Hecksteden match. Abstract (PMID 25663672) re-read in full; findings are paraphrases of it.
